English: Rock Shelter
A crude shelter of natural stone overhangs, offering basic protection for the first hermits seeking solitude in the mountains.
Mountain Hut
A simple wooden hut built with rough timber, providing shelter and space for meditation in the highlands.
Stone Hermitage
A sturdier dwelling of gathered stones, with a small altar, allowing a hermit to live and pray in relative comfort and safety.
Cliffside Cell
A solitary cell carved into the mountains edge, symbolizing the ascetics devotion and spiritual endurance.
Grotto Chapel
A humble chapel built into a natural cave, where a few disciples may gather for prayer and guidance.
Mountain Shrine
A revered shrine atop a high crag, drawing pilgrims and increasing the spiritual importance of the site.
High Hermitage
A fortified stone hermitage, housing a small community of anchorites and serving as a beacon of faith in the mountains.
Sanctuary in the Heights
A secluded sanctuary with multiple cells and a small library, attracting visiting monks and pilgrims seeking wisdom and peace.
Mountain Retreat
A well-fortified retreat with stone walls, scriptorium, and guesthouses for pilgrims, offering spiritual defense and fostering scholarship in the heights.
Mountain Monastery
A renowned monastery, renowned for its learning and piety, protected by formidable walls and known throughout Christendom as a bastion of faith and wisdom in the mountains.
